newsitem.title: USA: Input/Output sees weak earnings, stock tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Input/Output sees weak earnings, stock tumbles.

text.p: Input/Output, which makes seismic equipment for oil companies, on Thursday warned of disappointing results for its fiscal third quarter, triggering a sharp sell-off of its stock in heavy trading.
The stock fell $3.50 or almost 18 percent, to $16.125 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the biggest loser and one of the most active issues at mid-afternoon.
Input/Output said for the quarter ended Feb. 28, it expects earnings of $4.5 million to $6.5 million, or 10 cents to 15 cents per share, on revenues of $60 million to $65 million.
In the comparable year-ago quarter, the company reported net earnings of $11.8 million, or 27 cents per share, on revenues of $79.1 million.

Input/Output, based in Stafford, Texas, had 21 consecutive quarters of earnings growth until last fall, when a couple of large orders failed to be finalised on time. The stock then tumbled from $40 to $17.

The company said its latest results were hurt by competition in the land seismic equipment market, which was partially offset by demand for other systems. In addition, the company said that to date only one of the delayed sales from the second quarter had materialised.
"With the information we have today, we see reasonable demand for each of our product lines in the fourth quarter," said Chief Executive Officer Gary Owens.
Input/Output expects to report its final third-quarter results on March 18.
